Issues.Title: [release/10.0] Fix issue 15213: Bitmap finalized during Image.Save(Stream, ImageFormat) leaks native GDI+ memory
Issues.Body:
Backport of #15254 to release/10.0

Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/issues/15213

## Proposed changes

Within `CoreImageExtensions.Save(this IImage image, Stream stream, ...)` of `System.Private.Windows.GdiPlus`, wrap `GdipSaveImageToStream` in a try/finally block and call `GC.KeepAlive(image)` in the finally block.

## Customer Impact

The correction avoids abnormal native memory growth in `Save(Stream, ImageFormat)` under high-pressure/specific GC timings, reducing memory risks and potential stability issues in long-duration or batch image processing scenarios.

The impact on existing behavioral compatibility is minimal (only extending object survival to the end of the method), and should not change functional results or introduce visible behavioral differences.

- Yes - regression PR: #10783 or #10784

Issues.Title: Fix UpDown control layout when changing and resetting fonts
Issues.Body:
<!-- Please read CONTRIBUTING.md before submitting a pull request -->

Fixes #15331

## Root cause
Two issues in font-based autoscaling cause incorrect control bounds:

1. The parent’s cached autoscale factor remains available after font-change processing completes. An inheriting container, such as DomainUpDown or NumericUpDown, can reuse that stale factor when its own font changes, unexpectedly scaling its location and width.
2. Font-driven scaling skips all child container controls, assuming they will scale themselves when receiving the parent’s font-change notification. However, containers with an explicitly assigned font do not receive that notification unless required for DPI scaling. Consequently, resetting the form’s font leaves those controls at their previously scaled positions.


## Proposed changes

- Retain the parent’s autoscale factor only while processing and propagating a font change, restoring the previous factor afterward.
- Remove the cached-factor mutation from the autoscale-factor getter.
- Skip child containers during font-driven scaling only when they will receive a font-change notification and scale themselves.
- Scale containers with explicit fonts, including their descendants, through the normal recursive scaling path while preserving DPI-specific notification handling.
- Add regression coverage for both up-down controls, direct and nested parenting, inherited and explicit fonts, and different font-change/reset sequences.

## Customer Impact

- Prevents unexpected changes to the location and width of DomainUpDown and NumericUpDown when their fonts are changed after changing the form’s font.
- Ensures that controls with explicit fonts participate in parent font-based layout scaling, allowing their location and width to return appropriately when the form’s font is reset.
- Reduces manual layout correction after font edits in the WinForms Designer. No public API changes are introduced.

## Regression? 

-  Yes, it work well in .NET Framework

## Risk

- Minimal

<!-- end TELL-MODE -->

### Before

- Changing an up-down control’s font after changing the form’s font can unexpectedly change its location and width.
- If the up-down control has an explicit font, resetting the form’s font can leave it at its enlarged position. In the regression test, the control remains at (74,107) instead of returning to (40,50).

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e6c3235f-dc92-49f2-82b9-ffdd8803506d

### After

- Changing the up-down control’s own font preserves its location and width.
- Resetting the form’s font scales explicitly fonted up-down controls back to the expected location and width without clearing their explicit font.


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fde64fca-eb12-45f2-87db-5929571b47a3



## Test methodology <!-- How did you ensure quality? -->

- Add regression unit test
- Manual test

Issues.Title: Raise FormClosed once when the owner closes a modal dialog
Issues.Body:
Fixes #2451

## Proposed changes

- Let the modal message loop finish without raising the close events again after the owner has raised them.
- Reset close state at the start of each modal run and let the legacy `Closing` handler participate in cancellation before the owner commits the close.

## Customer Impact

The modal child raises one `FormClosed` event with `FormOwnerClosing` when its owner closes. Application cleanup subscribed to the event runs once.

## Regression?

The issue dates back to .NET Core 3.0 and .NET Framework 4.7.2.

## Risk

The change affects modal close sequencing. Legacy `Closing` now runs before an owner-driven modal close commits, where it can still cancel the operation.

## Test methodology

- Added upstream regression coverage for owner close, cancellation through both closing events, and reuse after overlapping closes.
- In an isolated Windows desktop, an equivalent IL patch on a private .NET 10.0.12 copy passed eight scenarios, including modeless and normal modal closes. The full repository source build and upstream test run are pending.
- Independent review identified stale closing state after overlapping closes. After the reset, the reviewer reran all eight scenarios successfully. `git diff --check` passed.

## Test environment

Windows 11 x64, .NET 10.0.12.

Issues.Title: [Suggestion] Shorten ToggleSwitch state-transition animations
Issues.Body:
### Background and motivation

The ToggleSwitch state-transition animation can feel too slow, making the control feel less responsive to user input. The feedback on PR #15270 suggests shortening state-transition animations.

This proposal is limited to the ToggleSwitch appearance used by CheckBox and RadioButton. It does not include their standard appearances or other button controls.

AnimatedToggleSwitchRenderer currently uses a 300 ms animation duration. We propose evaluating approximately 150 ms as an initial candidate to improve responsiveness while preserving the existing easing and smooth transitions.

The change should preserve continuous motion during rapid or reverse toggling and respect system settings that disable animations. Since the renderer shares its animation duration with hover and focus transitions, those interactions should also be validated.

### Will this feature affect UI controls?

Yes. This change affects only CheckBox and RadioButton controls using Appearance.ToggleSwitch, shortening their visual state-transition animations.

No changes to layout, sizing, public APIs, or logical checked-state behavior are intended. Standard CheckBox and RadioButton appearances and other UI controls will remain unaffected.

Because AnimatedToggleSwitchRenderer shares its animation duration with hover and focus transitions, those visual effects may also become faster and should be validated. System settings that disable animations will continue to be respected.

Issues.Title: Fix CheckedListBox check-state restoration when data binding changes the item count
Issues.Body:
<!-- Please read CONTRIBUTING.md before submitting a pull request -->

Fixes #15377

## Root cause
`CheckedListBox.RefreshItems` saves check states using the previous item count. The base refresh can repopulate the items from a data source with more entries, but the restoration loop previously used the new item count to index the old state array.

This causes an `IndexOutOfRangeException`. During `DataSource` assignment, the exception is caught internally and `DisplayMember` is cleared.

## Proposed changes

- Limit check-state restoration to the smaller of the saved state length and the refreshed item count.
- Preserve existing positional check-state restoration, additional items remain unchecked.
- Add regression tests for initial binding, rebinding, item-count changes, and check-state preservation, with and without a control handle.

<!-- We are in TELL-MODE the following section must be completed -->

## Customer Impact

- Prevents debugger interruptions caused by this first-chance exception during data binding.
- Keeps the configured `DisplayMember` intact, so bound items display the selected property rather than their `ToString()` values.

## Regression? 

- No, the same underlying issue can exist in .NET Framework, where a missing saved-state entry causes a `NullReferenceException` during unboxing. The array-based implementation instead throws an `IndexOutOfRangeException`

## Risk

- Minimal

## Screenshots <!-- Remove this section if PR does not change UI -->

### Before

[WinFormsApp23.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34566883/WinFormsApp23.zip)

Binding a larger data source throws an internal exception. If `DisplayMember` was assigned first, it can be reset, producing incorrect item labels. The debugger may break even though execution subsequently continues

Issues.Title: [release/11.0]  Backport of .NET 11 WinForms fixes to release/11.0
Issues.Body:
## Description

Backports seven WinForms fixes from main to release/11.0 for inclusion in the December 2026 .NET 11 servicing release.
These changes address several issues affecting control rendering, layout, DPI scaling, selection handling, and native resource management.

## Fixes

- dotnet/winforms#15325
- dotnet/winforms#15212
- dotnet/winforms#15361
- dotnet/winforms#15270
- dotnet/winforms#15207
- dotnet/winforms#15254
- ToggleSwitch state-transition animation improvements

##  Proposed Changes

This PR cherry-picks the following fixes:

1. **UpDown sizing and focus indicator (#15325)**
   - Fixes sizing issues and focus-indicator flickering in UpDown controls when using .NET 11 visual styles.
2. **DomainUpDown and NumericUpDown height (#15212)**
   - Fixes an issue where these controls incorrectly allow height changes instead of preserving their expected height in VisualStylesMode.Net11.
3. **ListBox selection handling (#15361)**
   - Fixes an IndexOutOfRangeException in ListBox.RefreshItems caused by a stale selected-item count cache.
4. **ToggleSwitch checked thumb color (#15270)**
   - Corrects the checked thumb color in both light and dark modes.
5. **UpDown DPI scaling (#15207)**
   - Fixes incorrect scaling of UpDown buttons when DPI changes.
6. **Bitmap native memory leak (#15254)**
   - Fixes a native GDI+ memory leak when a Bitmap is finalized during Image.Save(Stream, ImageFormat).
7. **ToggleSwitch animation improvements**
   - Shortens ToggleSwitch state-transition animations to improve responsiveness.

## Customer Impact

These fixes address issues that can affect applications running on .NET 11:

- **Visual and layout issues:** Incorrect control sizing, focus-indicator flickering, and inconsistent ToggleSwitch rendering can negatively affect the user experience.
- **High-DPI environments:** UpDown buttons may scale incorrectly when applications move between displays with different DPI settings.
- **Application reliability:** The ListBox issue can cause an IndexOutOfRangeException during item refresh operations.
- **Resource management:** The Bitmap issue can cause native GDI+ memory to remain allocated after the affected save operation.

The changes improve control rendering, layout consistency, DPI scaling, and application reliability. Existing applications will receive the fixes without requiring code changes.  Some visual and behavioral differences may be noticeable in affected controls, particularly those using .NET 11 visual styles.

## Regression?

**Partially.**

Several fixes address issues associated with the new .NET 11 visual styles, particularly control sizing, focus indicators, and ToggleSwitch rendering.
The remaining fixes address functional correctness, DPI scaling, and native resource management issues.
Not all seven issues have been confirmed as regressions introduced in .NET 11.

## Testing
All seven included fixes have been validated.

- Verified the fixes for all seven cherry-picked PRs.
- Confirmed that the corresponding GitHub issues are resolved.
- No new regression issues were identified during validation.

## Risk

**Minimal**

- These changes have already been merged into main.
- All seven fixes have been individually validated.
- No new regressions were identified during testing.
- Most changes are targeted fixes for specific control behaviors.
- The ListBox and Bitmap fixes affect functional behavior and native resource management, therefore, additional regression tests have been added.

Issues.Title: [release/11.0] Fix clipboard stalls during delayed rendering
Issues.Body: Backport of #15346 to release/11.0 /cc @Shyam-Gupta @davkean ## Issue Clipboard operations can stall and fail with `CLIPBRD_E_CANT_OPEN`. In a Visual Studio trace, Windows Clipboard User Service (`cbdhsvc`) was reading data through OLE and blocked in the delayed-rendering path: ```text CClipDataObject::GetData -> GetClipboardData -> xxxGetRenderData -> xxxInterSendMsgEx ``` ## Root Cause Windows was synchronously requesting clipboard data from the editor's UI thread (`WM_RENDERFORMAT`), while the service held the clipboard open. That UI thread was trying to replace the clipboard contents and sleeping between failed open attempts, so it could not answer the render request until retries were exhausted. ## Fix The retry wait now lets the UI thread answer sent messages, breaking that dependency without processing posted messages or queued input. Retry intervals and attempt limits remain unchanged. ## Customer Impact Clipboard operations in WinForms and WPF can recover from this contention instead of exhausting retries. ## Regression? Since .NET 11, WinForms runtime repo has started shipping an internal NuGet package, targeting .NET Framework, which includes the shared Clipboard and the new NRBF serializer/deserializer (the BinaryFormatter replacement). This package is consumed by VS AppLocal WPF which is shipped with VS and handles the Clipboard operations. This bug got introduced as part of that new package. Till Dev17, the Clipboard was handled by the old WPF code which didn’t have this issue. So, it can be considered as a regression. ## Risk All pending sent messages can run, not just clipboard-render requests. Their handlers can reenter application code and change clipboard or UI state. The retry deadline does not bound time spent inside a handler. ## Test methodology Mock OLE operations and private windows cover all five retry paths, delayed rendering, unrelated sent messages, nested calls, retry exhaustion, and posted-message preservation without touching the system clipboard. Also manually tested this with Visual Studio by continually holding down CTRL+X. ### Before ### After ## Test environment(s) Windows x64; .NET Framework 4.8.1 (x64 and x86) and .NET 12 (x64). ###### Microsoft Reviewers: [Open in CodeFlow](https://microsoft.github.io/open-pr/?codeflow=https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/15371)

Issues.Title: Fix Image.Width/Height DefaultValue (false -> 0) for dotnet/runtime#126265
Issues.Body:
Fixes dotnet/runtime#126265

## Proposed changes

**What:** Change `DefaultValue` metadata for `System.Drawing.Image.Width` and `System.Drawing.Image.Height` from `DefaultValue(false)` to `DefaultValue(0)`.

**Why:** `Width`/`Height` are `int` properties but declared `[DefaultValue(false)]`. Metadata consumers that read the default via `TypeDescriptor`/`PropertyDescriptor.Attributes` receive a `Boolean` value. When `Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi` (or `System.Text.Json.Schema.JsonSchema`) generates a schema from a model containing an `Image?` property, it does `UnboxOnWrite<int>(defaultValue)` and throws:

```
InvalidCastException: Unable to cast object of type 'System.Boolean' to type 'System.Int32'.
  at System.Text.Json.JsonSerializer.UnboxOnWrite<T>(object value)
  at Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi.JsonNodeSchemaExtensions.ApplyDefaultValue(...)
```

This is the exact failure reported in dotnet/runtime#126265.

**How:**
- `src/System.Drawing.Common/src/System/Drawing/Image.cs`: `Width`/`Height` `[DefaultValue(false)]` → `[DefaultValue(0)]`.
- `src/System.Drawing.Common/src/Special/NotSupported.cs` (netstandard stub): same fix for the two stub properties.
- `src/System.Drawing.Common/tests/System/Drawing/ImageTests.cs`: add `ImageDimensionProperty_DefaultValueIsZero` theory asserting `TypeDescriptor` default is `(int)0` for both properties.
- `src/System.Drawing.Common/src/CompatibilitySuppressions.xml`: intentional `CP0015` suppressions for both properties across `net10.0`/`netstandard2.0` baselines (`[T:System.ComponentModel.DefaultValueAttribute]` target).

> **Duplicate note:** Draft PR #14895 (`Fix Image dimension DefaultValue metadata`, https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/14895) covers the same issue and was verified present before opening this PR. This PR is opened per contributor request as a ready-for-review submission of commit `660b4b1` (fix: Correct Image.Width/Height DefaultValue metadata). Please close one as duplicate.

## Customer Impact

- Metadata consumers that read `Image.Width`/`Height` defaults via `TypeDescriptor`/`PropertyDescriptor.Attributes` no longer receive a Boolean default for `int` properties.
- Fixes `InvalidCastException` in metadata/schema consumers such as OpenAPI generation (`Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi` `ApplyDefaultValue` path).
- No runtime behavior change: property values, API surface unchanged; only design-time metadata corrected.

## Regression?

- No. This corrects invalid design-time metadata; property values and API surface are unchanged.

## Risk

- Low. Production change is limited to two `DefaultValue` attributes (+ netstandard stub parity) and is covered by a focused `TypeDescriptor` regression test. ApiCompat `CP0015` suppressions added intentionally; no API signature change.

## Test methodology

- Built `System.Drawing.Common` and `System.Drawing.Common.Tests` with the repo-pinned .NET 11 toolchain.
- New regression test `ImageTests.ImageDimensionProperty_DefaultValueIsZero` (2 cases, Width + Height): 2 passed, 0 failed.
- Full `System.Drawing.Common.Tests` suite: **5292 passed, 0 failed** (xUnit, Windows x64).
- Verified fix direction: `TypeDescriptor.GetProperties(typeof(Image))["Width"/"Height"]` default is now `System.Int32 0`, not `System.Boolean false`.

## Edge cases

- `TypeDescriptor` on abstract `Image` (property not abstract): `PropertyDescriptor.Attributes[typeof(DefaultValueAttribute)]` returns `DefaultValueAttribute(0)`; test asserts both `IsType` and value `0` to guard against future type drift.
- netstandard stub (`NotSupported.cs`): patched identically so non-Windows stub contract matches Windows implementation; ApiCompat baselines suppressed intentionally (3 suppression sets: `net10.0` baseline, `netstandard2.0` vs `net462`, `netstandard2.0` baseline).
- Web API/OpenAPI repro shape (`WeatherForecast.Image`): default lookup now succeeds without cast; consumer unaffected beyond fix.

## Test environment(s)

- Windows x64
- .NET SDK `11.0.100-preview.6.26359.118`
- Test runtime `11.0.0-rc.1.26411.119`

Issues.Title: [release/10.0] Add opt-in native clipboard text fallback for WPF
Issues.Body:
Fixes dotnet/wpf#11968 in conjunction with the corresponding WPF changes.

## Proposed changes

• Add an internal, default-disabled policy allowing WPF to opt into native clipboard text fallback. WinForms explicitly remains opted out.
• Compose the original managed source with a captured native OLE reader. Legacy and typed retrieval remain managed-first, with fallback restricted to Text, UnicodeText, and OEMText .
• Preserve custom-payload identity, managed format enumeration, and writes. Add six regression cases covering WinForms clipboard behavior before and after flushing.

## Customer Impact

• Enables WPF to restore Windows text synthesis when managed clipboard sources disable automatic conversion, addressing missing text availability and retrieval reported in dotnet/wpf#11968.
• Preserves existing WinForms behavior: unflushed clipboard data retains managed conversion semantics, while flushed data exposes Windows-synthesized formats.

## Regression

• Yes — supports fixing a .NET 10 WPF regression. No intentional WinForms behavior change.

## Risk

• Low for WinForms because the fallback policy remains disabled. Moderate for opted-in consumers because shared clipboard composition and retrieval paths change. Fallback is limited to plain-text formats and retains the captured proxy’s owning adapters.
